ownership_and_barrier_attack.boundedness_result: The recurrence really is bounded to B live descriptors, but B is not a byte-capacity or memory-port specification.

streaming_sensitivity_not_a_corrected_re.interpretation: This conservative schedule is a sensitivity bound, not a replacement headline. It proves that the selected B3 point and exact ratios depend materially on a streaming/dual-port/forwarding contract that the aggregate recurrence does not encode.

findings.title: The selected B3 cycles require an unmodeled same-descriptor streaming or dual-port contract
findings.observation: The recurrence starts PWP at max(pwp_free, fill_start), not at fill_end or at per-token availability. On the exact B3 trace, 49,521 of 69,120 descriptors start PWP before descriptor fill completes, with a maximum 4,049-cycle lead. The result names descriptor/result banks but does not define simultaneous descriptor write, PWP input read, result write, correction read, forwarding, arbitration, or token-level backpressure.
findings.impact: 133,326,568 cycles and the 2.636228947x/1.841237749x ratios are exact for the aggregate recurrence but are not yet implementable-cycle admissions. A conservative fill-complete sensitivity reaches 144,690,917 cycles, reducing the two ratios to 2.429174x and 1.696623x; it also makes B4 more useful. This sensitivity is not claimed as the correct hardware result, only proof that the missing interface matters.
findings.required_fix: Define a token-level producer/PWP/correction handshake and a concrete bank port map. Replay exact per-row PWP arrivals with stalls and assert no consumer reads an unwritten descriptor/result. Re-run B2/B3/B4 after that model before freezing B3 for RTL.

findings.title: The combined ratios inherit an unimplemented already-sparse-mask producer
findings.observation: M141 feeds one ordered K4 descriptor per cycle from M140, whose frozen contract explicitly says the already-sparse 16-bit mask producer is unimplemented and complete-row losslessness is unproved. The M141 contract lists the K4 descriptorizer but does not carry this upstream cost/latency boundary into its headline cycle composition.
findings.impact: The candidate can receive a preformed sparse mask while the M132 compact256 numerator pays the older raw-source fill recurrence. If real mask formation, buffering, or row ordering stalls the descriptor/PWP streams, 2.636228947x is optimistic even before physical frequency and macro costs.
findings.required_fix: Implement or cycle-model the mask producer from the same frozen input boundary, include its latency/backpressure in both numerator and candidate, and prove complete row/partition losslessness before describing the ratio as a complete module schedule.

findings.title: Three banks bound descriptor count but not storage bytes or ports
findings.observation: Independent sweeping confirms peak live descriptor occupancy exactly 2/3/4 and no same-bank refill before declared release. B3 nevertheless permits two completed PWP results to wait for correction, a maximum PWP service extent of 6,355 512-bit tokens, and a maximum wait of 5,289 cycles. The model never defines the stored object, capacity, banking, read/write ports, or whether the result is streamed or materialized.
findings.impact: The no-unbounded-FIFO statement is valid only at descriptor granularity. A conditional materialized-beat illustration is 406,720 bytes per maximum-size bank and 1,220,160 bytes for three equally provisioned banks; actual storage may be smaller or larger depending on the missing representation.
findings.minimal_fix: Freeze descriptor and result record widths, per-bank depths, simultaneous port requirements, spill/backpressure behavior, and macro mapping. Select B3 against B2/B4 using cycle-area-energy Pareto results rather than descriptor count alone.

findings.title: The reported B3/B4 overlap-cycle diagnostic undercounts true engine overlap
findings.observation: The analyzer intersects each PWP interval only with `previous_correction_start..correction_free`. That is exact for B2, but a B3/B4 PWP interval can span multiple queued correction intervals. Independent interval-union arithmetic gives B3 111,381,529 overlap cycles versus reported 61,101,162, a 50,280,367 undercount; B4 is 113,202,267 versus 43,615,395, a 69,586,872 undercount.
findings.impact: Candidate cycles and the three cited ratios remain unchanged because they do not use this counter, but the overlap diagnostic is unsafe for architectural explanation, utilization, or energy attribution.
findings.minimal_fix: Compute intersection length across the full ordered PWP and correction active-interval unions, or remove the diagnostic from evidence until corrected.

findings.title: The B3 selection text confuses speedup with cycle reduction
findings.observation: B3/B2 is 1.094452930x, but the actual cycle reduction is 1 - 133,326,568/145,919,653 = 8.630150%, not 9.45%. B4/B3 is 1.014061570x and its cycle reduction is 1.386658%.
findings.impact: Saying the third bank removes 9.45% cycle time overstates the reduction and makes the storage trade look better.
findings.minimal_fix: Use either `1.09445x speedup` or `8.63015% fewer cycles`; keep speedup ratio and reduction percentage separate.

findings.title: The window barrier drains service engines but intentionally permits producer lookahead
findings.observation: All 160 barriers block PWP and correction service correctly. `producer_end` is not advanced by commit, so B3 fills up to three next-window descriptors during the preceding commit; 474 such fills occur. Ownership keeps this bounded and no PWP service crosses the barrier.
findings.impact: This is not a cycle error if descriptor metadata is window-independent and banks do not alias accumulator commit state, but a simplistic RTL interpretation of a total window barrier can diverge from the model.
findings.minimal_fix: State explicitly that only PWP/correction/controller drain, assert producer lookahead is at most B, and prove descriptor/result banks are disjoint from accumulator state consumed during commit.

findings.title: The r1 correction receipt names an R2 successor while the admitted artifact is r3
findings.observation: The correction file status says `SUPERSEDED_BY_R2` and lists `r2_requirements`, whereas the frozen analyzer/result/contract are M141r3. The numerical correction itself is exact: (8-3)*8,271,296 = 41,356,480 excess tokens.
findings.impact: The lineage is numerically auditable but the supersession label is ambiguous and can cause a reviewer to search for a nonexistent or unstated r2 evidence point.
findings.minimal_fix: Add a non-destructive lineage overlay that identifies r1 invalid identities, any r2 disposition, and the exact r3 analyzer/result/contract identities.

ratio_scope.2_636228947x: Combined same-clock heldout module-cycle ratio of B3 K4 fill plus PWP/correction overlap versus the older M132 compact256 serial recurrence; not an overlap-only, physical, full-network, or system result.
ratio_scope.1_841237749x: Combined same-clock heldout module-cycle ratio versus M132 dualrow512 serial service; not matched-frequency or system speedup.
ratio_scope.8_361900143x: B3 same-clock service-island ratio versus the fixed8 baseline; not full-network, end-to-end, physical, or measured-frequency speedup.
ratio_scope.admitted_after_review: All three ratios are independently arithmetic-exact under the frozen aggregate recurrence, but not implementation-admitted until both P1 items close.

ordered_actions: Replace aggregate fill-start PWP launch with an exact token-level arrival/backpressure replay and explicit bank port schedule.
Bring the already-sparse-mask producer into the same cycle boundary and prove complete row losslessness.
Define stored records, per-bank bytes/depth/ports, and B2/B3/B4 cycle-area-energy Pareto cost.
Correct the B3/B4 overlap-cycle diagnostic and speedup-versus-reduction wording.
Freeze a lineage overlay from invalid r1 through final r3 before further derivative milestones.
Only then implement the selected bounded handoff and verify with VCS/SVA; retain all physical/system/headline flags false until matched Synopsys and composed trace evidence.
claim_boundary: M141r3 is reproducible and its heldout aggregate recurrence/work arithmetic is strong. It does not yet admit a realizable three-bank schedule, RTL, buffer/macro PPA, matched frequency, physical speedup, full-network speedup, system speedup, DATE headline, or best-paper claim.
